findings.failure_path: The replaced paragraph drops the 'The matrix is a ceiling, not a floor' invariant, including 'Absence is not permission': anything irreversible, destructive, production-affecting, or of unclear authority preserves state and asks even with no row of its own. With that default removed, an action not listed in the matrix (e.g. a registry or infra mutation invoked as part of an 'established publication workflow') has no stated stop rule and can be read as covered by the release goal, contradicting the acceptance item that missing resource authority and destructive operations are not granted by a release goal.
findings.smallest_fix: Re-add the default sentence to the rewritten paragraph: unlisted actions acquire no authority by analogy, and anything irreversible, destructive, production-affecting, or of unclear authority preserves state and asks.

findings.failure_path: The 'Play manual production job' row changes from 'Yes' (explicit authorization required) to 'Covered only for the established requested release flow and caller's resource authority'. A user request to publish an npm patch now textually covers playing manual production jobs, an irreversible production-affecting action outside the stated intent (npm publication through the existing OIDC workflow). Nothing in the diff bounds 'established flow' to the publication pipeline.
findings.smallest_fix: Restrict this row to jobs that are part of the named publication pipeline for the requested release, and keep explicit authorization for any other manual production job.

findings.failure_path: New pins assert only the added goal-authority sentences; no pin retains the matrix-ceiling / 'Absence is not permission' invariant or the production-job gating. Deleting those safeguards (as this diff does) leaves the suite green, so the tests would still pass with the risky behavior enabled.
findings.smallest_fix: Add an assert_contains pin on release-coordination/SKILL.md for the retained absence-is-not-permission sentence once it is restored.

concern_results.conclusion: The goal-scoped authorization rewrite is internally consistent across AGENTS.md, session-start.md, docs, release-coordination and worktree-isolation, and the version bump to 0.15.4 is applied to both package.json and package-lock.json. Acceptance items about narrow/preparation-only scope are textually preserved (F13 rewritten to a pending-review negative, F37/F40 negatives added). One gap: the release matrix rewrite drops the previously explicit 'absence is not permission' default for unlisted actions, which is required behavior absent from the diff.

No runtime permission mechanism, hook, or credential is modified, and the host-guard non-bypass language is retained and pinned. However the matrix now marks 'Play manual production job' and production tag push as covered by a release request, and removes the ceiling paragraph's catch-all that anything irreversible/destructive/production-affecting or of unclear authority preserves state and asks. That is a real loosening of production-mutation gating beyond the stated npm-publication intent.

Repair-before-handoff is well specified: pre-final-continuation-gate now requires citing failure output, repair attempts or evidence repair is unsafe, and the residual blocker before a blocked verdict; refactoring-discipline defines what counts as a material tradeoff and preserves stop/status-only precedence. Partial-blocker behavior (continue independent authorized work) is stated in both places.

The escalation-pins fixture now copies docs/ and AGENTS.md, matching the new assertions that read those paths, so the pre-control would no longer fail spuriously. New pins assert the added rule sentences and would fail if those lines were deleted. But no pin covers the removed 'Absence is not permission' / matrix-ceiling invariant, so the safety regression above is a behavior change the suite still passes on.

No CLI contract, hook, dependency, workflow, or package description change; only prose and a patch version bump. The worktree-isolation merge protocol remains canonical and the session-start layer still points to it, keeping the two-layer contract in sync.

Patch 0.15.4 is prepared consistently; publication path still runs through the tag-checked OIDC workflow described in docs/npm-release.md, and version immutability plus separately-scoped deprecation/unpublish are preserved. Rollback for the policy text itself is a revert; no irreversible artifact is created by the diff.

Blocked-status reporting now carries mandatory evidence (failure output, attempts, residual blocker), and merge execution still requires presenting URL, source→target, head SHA, and CI state. Diagnosis visibility is improved rather than reduced.
